title: U.S. Soccer CEO: USMNT’s Mauricio Pochettino ‘100%’ focused on World Cup despite Milan meeting
content:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson said that Mauricio Pochettino has been “very focused” on both the 2026 World Cup and the “long-term success” of U.S. Soccer, even after meeting with representatives from AC Milan last week.

The Athletic reported Thursday that Pochettino met with the Italian club before joining up with the U.S. men’s national team for their World Cup camp, which opened Wednesday at the U.S. Soccer Federation’s new national training center.

Batson, speaking to reporters while the USMNT trained over his shoulder — and while Pochettino prowled on the side of a drill, shouting at players, “Go go go go go!” — indicated that he was not bothered by the meeting with Milan. He said that Pochettino had been “transparent about club interest” since he first agreed to take charge of the USMNT in 2024, and that “there’s been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported.”

Batson also indicated that extending Pochettino’s contract beyond this summer’s World Cup remained a possibility.

“Mauricio and the entire team has been incredibly transparent the entire process,” Batson said. “Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and [his staff] join. He had standing offers from other places to come, and he wanted to be here. He’s a big believer in what we’re doing at U.S. Soccer, he’s a big believer in soccer in America and he’s a big believer in this men’s team.

“When you have top-class talent, whether it’s salespeople, whether it’s marketing people, or whether it’s coaches, other organizations want them. Throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent, they’ve been great partners, and we’re, of course, excited about the summer.”

Speaking prior to training, two USMNT players also said they did not care about Pochettino’s meeting with Milan.

“It doesn’t bother us,” winger Tim Weah said. “I’m someone that lives in present day, and right now he’s here and we’re working with him. It’s an amazing feeling having such a prestigious coach coaching us.

“Whatever he decides to do after is what the coach decides, and we’re here to support him. He’s here to support us, and we’re just living in the present and making sure that we do our job.”

Midfielder Tyler Adams added: “Our focus has to be here on the World Cup. As [with] any manager or player — like, there’s [players] in contract situations right now that have to figure out what to do, either before the World Cup, after the World Cup. It’s gonna be the same deal with coaches.

“He’s fully present with us every single day, finding ways to make us better, focusing on the trainings, just as we are,” Adams concluded.

An hour later, that was evident. Pochettino had requested that U.S. Soccer staffers, who now work out of the headquarters at the national training center, be allowed to watch training. He spoke to them before Thursday’s session. More than a hundred of them then looked down from a second-floor balcony overlooking the training pitch as Thursday’s session began.

Before the players arrived on the “superpitch,” a vast grass pitch that fits three full-size fields, Pochettino chatted with Batson for a while before players arrived. At one point, he looked up to the staff and led a “U-S-A” chant.

Batson said that one of his first thoughts upon seeing The Athletic’s report on Thursday morning was that, on Wednesday night, Pochettino, his top assistant Jesús Perez, U.S. Soccer chief operating officer Dan Halfrich and Batson “were actually the last people to leave the national training center,” and their meeting “was all about the Olympics, was about our youth teams, about coaching education.”

Batson was also asked about the possibility of re-signing Pochettino for a second World Cup cycle. “We’ve had a number of very long discussions around what the next four years could look like,” Batson said. “We’re excited, and they’re excited, but of course we got to focus on the summer.”

That was his main message, and he said he believes that Pochettino’s head is where it needs to be.

“I’m confident that Mauricio and team are 100 percent focused on this summer,” Batson said. “They’re excited, they’re among the first people here this morning, they’re the last to leave last night.”

Baton was also grilled Thursday about the void atop U.S. Soccer’s sporting department, which has seemingly complicated discussions about the future of the USMNT after Pochettino’s contract expires post-World Cup.

Sporting director Matt Crocker left the federation last month to take a similar job in Saudi Arabia. Crocker’s prior relationship with Pochettino helped lead the previous USMNT coaching search to Pochettino in 2024. With Crocker gone, it’s been unclear who will be in charge of making a decision on Pochettino’s future or hiring the next coach.

Batson, though, said he felt confident in the current executive team’s ability to make decisions for the short and long term. The sporting department is being led by Helfrich, the recently-hired COO who has his hands on a wide variety of U.S. Soccer initiatives and activities.

“We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams,” Batson said. “And so as a part of that, we have plans for renewals, we have plans for interims, and we have plans for replacements — because you never know what’s going to happen. It’s a global sport, lots going on, and so that’s a standard part of us growing up as U.S. soccer.”

Batson also said that a few months ago, he and U.S. Soccer began “thinking about the long-term structure of our soccer organization. We’ve grown 3x over the last four years. … As a part of our ability to deliver on our long-term goals, we knew we were gonna have to evolve our soccer organization.”

“There are a few things that have come out of that review,” he continued. The two main takeaways, he said, were:

He also voiced support for executives and staffers who are already in the door at U.S. Soccer.

“So,” he concluded, “I would not expect a like-for-like” replacement for Crocker.

He said the federation was actively working toward a “new structure.”

As for the post-World Cup coaching search, Batson was asked specifically whether there had been outreach to Pep Guardiola, who recently left Manchester City, or to Jürgen Klopp.

“We have been focused on this summer,” Batson said, “and that’s been all of our priority.”
